title: Exceptional pretzel knots are not algebraically slice
summary: We consider the three-strand pretzel knot $P_a=P(a,-a-2,-(a+1)^2/2)$ and prove that, when $a\equiv1\pmod4$, its Alexander polynomial fails the Fox--Milnor condition. The same remains true after adding any number of opposite odd parameter pairs $q,-q$ and reordering the parameters. Combined with work of Kim--Lee--Song, this gives the same conclusion for every odd $a\ge3$. In particular, no knot in Lecuona's exceptional family is algebraically or topologically slice. Together with earlier work of Lecuona, Miller, and Kim--Lee--Song, this completes the slice--ribbon and topological-sliceness…
